TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Bounds for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We provide non-asymptotic bounds for the expected mean squared error (EMSE) of KernelSHAP, and show that the number of necessary value-function evaluations is dictated by the "influence" of the Shapley value to be estimated. Specifically, let $\tau_j = \min_{S:j \in S^+, S\in \cup} k(S)(v(S\setminus \{j\})-v(S))$, where the minimum is taken over all subsets that include feature $j$. We derive an upper bound for the EMSE of KernelSHAP that is proportional to $1/\tau_j^2$ (whp), showing that features with small $\tau_j$ require larger sample sizes to achieve the same accuracy level.
CONTROLS: For baselines, we compare to post-hoc feature perturbation methods, over-sampling the subset sums, and the naive Monte Carlo method.
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: We expect our bound will provide valuable insights into the sample efficiency of KernelSHAP, and show that it exhibits exponential concentration of the EMSE as a function of $j$, which underlines its over-performance in small-density regimes.

TITLE: LeverageSHAP Extensions and Variations
PROPOSAL: We propose to extend, modify and analyze several variants of LeverageSHAP, which samples the rows of the regression problem according to their statistical leverage scores. We present several alterations to the sampling distribution, including exponential sampling, in which rows are sampled with probability proportional to $\exp(t \cdot \bm{x}^\top \bm{Z} \bm{x})$. Additionally, we explore the use of anti- leverage scores, and investigate how these altered methods compare in terms of simulation efficiency and prediction accuracy to existing methods like KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. We predict that one of the proposed methods will offer a tradeoff between competing with the state-of-the-art of LeverageSHAP's efficiency, and retaining KernelSHAP's speed advantages.
CONTROLS: For control, we compare against LeverageSHAP, and the replay buffer method for parameter-free regression estimation. We run careful experiments on real-world datasets where statistical leverage scores are close to zero. 
COST: 388800
PREDICTION: We expect that some variation of the LeverageSHAP approach will emerge as a new alternative to KernelSHAP.

TITLE: Model-Agnostic Interpretable Method with Regularization
PROPOSAL: We introduce a new model-agnostic interpretable method, MIReg, which leverages the principle of regularization to incorporate interpretability constraints. By minimizing a objective function that balances the prediction error and an interpretability term, MIReg produces globally interpretable results that align with the model's predictions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of MIReg on various real-world datasets, including image classification, text classification, and regression problems.
CONTROLS: We compare MIReg with state-of-the-art methods, such as SHAP, LIME, and Anchors, using metrics like accuracy, F1-score, mean squared error, and interpretability metrics like feature importance and mutual information.
COST: 576000
PREDICTION: MIReg is expected to provide a trade-off between model accuracy and interpretability, making it a versatile tool for various real-world applications.

TITLE: Multi-Fidelity Sampling for Efficient Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-fidelity sampling approach for efficient Shapley value estimation. By adaptively sampling the most informative subsets and using a learned surrogate model to approximate the Shapley values, our method significantly reduces the computational cost while maintaining high accuracy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of speed and accuracy.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with sampling-based methods like KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, as well as model-based methods like LIME and Anchors.
COST: 864000
PREDICTION: Our multi-fidelity sampling approach is expected to become a new state-of-the-art method for efficient Shapley value estimation, making it suitable for large-scale real-world applications.

TITLE: Libertarian Fairness and Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: We investigate the connection between libertarian fairness and Shapley values, and propose a novel framework for quantifying and addressing fairness issues in Shapley-based explanations. Our framework is based on a reinterpretation of the Shapley value as a measure of individual contribution to the overall team performance, and provides a way to identify and mitigate unfairness in the explanations.
CONTROLS: We compare our framework with existing fairness metrics and methods, and evaluate its performance on various real-world datasets.
COST: 720000
PREDICTION: Our framework is expected to provide a new perspective on fairness in Shapley-based explanations, and offer a practical tool for addressing fairness issues in real-world applications.

TITLE: Scalable Shapley Value Computation via Sketching and Streaming
PROPOSAL: We propose a scalable and efficient method for computing Shapley values via sketching and streaming. Our approach uses a small set of random projections to summarize the input data, and then uses a streaming algorithm to compute the Shapley values. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on large-scale datasets and show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of speed and accuracy.
CONTROLS: We compare our method with existing methods for Shapley value computation, including exact and approximate methods, and evaluate its performance on various real-world datasets.
COST: 1008000
PREDICTION: Our scalable method is expected to become a new state-of-the-art approach for computing Shapley values, making it suitable for large-scale real-world applications.

TITLE: Unifying and Generalizing Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: We provide a unifying framework for Shapley value estimation, encompassing various existing methods as special cases. Our framework is based on a game-theoretic interpretation of Shapley values as a solution to a constrained optimization problem. We derive a generalization of the Shapley value estimation problem, which allows us to compare and contrast existing methods in a principled way. Our results provide a deeper understanding of the Shapley value estimation problem and shed light on the relative strengths and weaknesses of different methods.
CONTROLS: We compare our framework with existing methods for Shapley value estimation, including exact and approximate methods, and evaluate its performance on various real-world datasets.
COST: 1209600
PREDICTION: Our unifying framework is expected to become a new foundation for Shapley value estimation, providing a more comprehensive and nuanced understanding of the problem and its relationships to existing methods.

TITLE: Long-Term Temporal Change Description with Temporally-Constrained MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune the multimodal large language model (MM-LM) BERT-LMADA+ with a temporally-constrained objective that encourages the model to capture long-range temporal dynamics in satellite image time series. This is achieved by adding a temporal coherence loss to the MM-LM training objective. Specifically, we compute the cosine similarity between encoded representations of consecutive images and add a loss term that encourages this similarity to be high for images close in time, and low for images far in time. We evaluate this approach on the Temporal Change Captioning (TCC) dataset and compete with the current state-of-the-art, TCC-XLM, which is neither temporally-constrained nor optimized for land use change.
CONTROLS: TCC-XLM, static image-to-text, captioning baseline
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: We expect this temporally-constrained MM-LM to improve upon the static baseline, possibly by a large margin, but may struggle to match or exceed the performance of state-of-the-art TCC-XLM.

TITLE: Memory-Augmented Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Design a satellite image time series forecasting model that leverages external memory to store and update the history of observed changes. This is achieved by combining a convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction with a memory-augmented neural network (MAM) that maintains a vector representation of the observed sequence. The MAM module uses attention mechanisms to selectively update this vector representation at each time step, allowing it to capture long-range temporal dependencies. We evaluate this approach on the Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting (SITSF) dataset and compare with state-of-the-art forecasters.
CONTROLS: Basic Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), Temporal Residual Network (TRN)
COST: 135000
PREDICTION: We expect this memory-augmented model to outperform the TCN and TRN baselines due to its ability to store and update the history of observed changes, but may face challenges in handling irregular sampling rates or large gaps in the time series.

TITLE: Forecasting Temporally Consistent Satellite Images with Semantics-Guided Diffusion
PROPOSAL: Develop a semantics-guided diffusion model for satellite image time series forecasting that captures the temporal evolution of changes. This is achieved by incorporating a semantics-aware prior that encourages the generated images to be consistent with the historical sequence. Specifically, we use a variational autoencoder (VAE) to encode the historical images, and then use a diffusion model to generate new images that are consistent with the VAE's learned semantics. We evaluate this approach on the SITSF dataset and compare with state-of-the-art forecasters.
CONTROLS: Diffusion model baseline, VAE-based generation baseline
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: We expect this semantics-guided diffusion model to generate forecast images that are not only temporally consistent but also semantically plausible, and potentially outperform the diffusion model baseline. However, it may rely heavily on the quality of the VAE's learned semantics and face challenges in handling large gaps in the time series.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Long-Term Temporal Change Description with Temporally-Constrained MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Revise the temporally-constrained MM-LM by incorporating an additional task to jointly predict the temporal order of the images. This is achieved by adding a supervised learning objective that predicts the temporal interval between consecutive images, and incorporating this information into the temporal coherence loss. Specifically, we compute the temporal coherence loss as a function of the predicted temporal interval, and optimize the model to capture temporal patterns at multiple time scales.
CONTROLS: Original temporally-constrained MM-LM, conventional image classification baseline
COST: 108000
PREDICTION: We expect this revised model to improve upon the original temporally-constrained MM-LM by capturing temporal patterns at multiple time scales, and potentially outperform the conventional image classification baseline. However, it may face challenges in handling irregular sampling rates or large gaps in the time series.

TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a framework to evaluate the temporal consistency of satellite image time series forecasting models. This is achieved by introducing a set of metrics that quantify the consistency of the forecasted sequence with the historical sequence, as well as with the underlying temporal patterns and trends. We evaluate these metrics on the SITSF dataset and apply them to the semantics-guided diffusion model.
CONTROLS: Perceptual quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM), distance-based metrics (L1, L2)
COST: 72000
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed framework to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the temporal consistency of satellite image time series forecasting models, and potentially reveal strengths and weaknesses of existing approaches. However, it may face challenges in balancing the trade-off between accuracy and interpretability of the proposed metrics.

TITLE: Uncovering Causal Narrative of Temporal Change in Satellite Imagery
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to automatically extract causal narrative of temporal changes in satellite imagery by leveraging the temporal change description capabilities of the temporally-constrained MM-LM. This is achieved by fine-tuning the model to predict causal relationships between events and temporal patterns, and using these relationships to identify the underlying drivers of change. We evaluate this approach on the Atlantic Forest dataset and compare with human-annotated ground truth.
CONTROLS: Temporally-constrained MM-LM, causal graph learning baseline
COST: 162000
PREDICTION: We expect this method to provide insights into the causal narrative of temporal changes in satellite imagery, and potentially identify new relationships between events and temporal patterns. However, it may face challenges in handling complex and conflicting causal relationships, and require large amounts of annotated data to train the model effectively.

TITLE: satelliteMLM: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal Dataset for Satellite Imagery
PROPOSAL: Collect and annotate a large-scale multi-modal dataset for satellite imagery, including tens of thousands of images, corresponding text descriptions, and temporal information. This dataset will serve as a benchmark for multi-modal satellite image understanding and forecasting tasks, and provide a basis for training and evaluating the proposed models. We will make the dataset publicly available to the research community.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 270000
PREDICTION: We expect satelliteMLM to become a valuable resource for the satellite image understanding and forecasting research community, and potentially enable new breakthroughs in the field. However, it may require significant effort and resources to collect and annotate the dataset, and potentially raise issues related to data privacy and security.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Memory-Augmented Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Re-design the memory-augmented neural network (MAM) module in the satellite image time series forecasting model to use a more efficient and scalable architecture, such as a hierarchical or recursive graph-based structure. This should improve the model's ability to store and update the history of observed changes, and reduce the computational cost of training and inference.
CONTROLS: Original memory-augmented model, graph-based neural network baseline
COST: 202500
PREDICTION: We expect the revised model to exhibit improved performance and efficiency, and potentially outperform the graph-based neural network baseline. However, it may require significant modifications to the model's architecture and training procedure, and potentially introduce new challenges related to model interpretability and explainability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Forget: Adaptive Temporal Abstraction in Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a model that can learn to forget and abstract temporal information adaptively, instead of relying on a fixed temporal resolution or granularity. This is achieved by incorporating a learning-based module that selects which temporal information to retain and which to forget, based on the task requirements and data characteristics. We evaluate this approach on the satelliteMLM dataset and compare with state-of-the-art forecasters.
CONTROLS: Memory-augmented model with fixed temporal resolution, attention-based model
COST: 225000
PREDICTION: We expect the adaptive temporal abstraction model to outperform the memory-augmented model with fixed temporal resolution, and potentially match or exceed the performance of the attention-based model. However, it may require significant effort to design and train the learning-based module, and potentially introduce new challenges related to model interpretability and explainability.

TITLE: Forecasting Temporally Consistent Satellite Images with Semantics-Guided Diffusion
PROPOSAL: Re-design the semantics-guided diffusion model to incorporate a more robust and flexible architecture, such as a neural ODE (Ordinary Differential Equation) or a hierarchical Bayesian neural network. This should improve the model's ability to capture complex temporal dynamics and semantically meaningful patterns in the data, and reduce the risk of overfitting or mode collapse.
CONTROLS: Original semantics-guided diffusion model, neural ODE baseline
COST: 247500
PREDICTION: We expect the revised model to outperform the original semantics-guided diffusion model and potentially match or exceed the performance of the neural ODE baseline. However, it may require significant modifications to the model's architecture and training procedure, and potentially introduce new challenges related to model interpretability and explainability.

TITLE:  Investigating Adapter Parameters for Online Traffic Flow Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will extend popular online traffic flow forecasting models, such as Spatiotemporal Recurrent Neural Networks (STRNN) and Univariate or Multivariate SARIMA-GRU, by replacing pre-defined adapter layers with learnable adapter modules that have significantly fewer parameters. The Learnable Adapter Module will have two fully connected neural networks with 10 and 5 neurons respectively and two ReLU activation layers.

COST: 25200
PREDICTION: We expect the learnable adapter model to obtain better forecasting performance than the baselines, particularly in scenarios with rapid changes in traffic flow patterns due to road construction, accidents, or special events. However, this approach might fail for models with architectures that are too interdependent or require significant adapter specialization.  We will analyze which characteristics of the models lead to failure by abating number of neurons in learnable adapter.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE:  Safe Learning for Online Traffic Forecasting with Gradient Regularization
PROPOSAL: We will incorporate a gradient regularization term into the online update scheme to help the model adapt to changing traffic patterns while avoiding abrupt changes in the forecasts. The term will be derived from the training data using a risk-sensitive objective, specifically Minimax Risk Sensitive (MRS) regularizer which can help detect outliers and improve noise robustness.
CONTROLS: Control experiments will be conducted using standard gradient descent, gradient clipping, and weight decay to compare the performance of the proposed method with existing techniques that address concept drift and large gradients.
COST: 37150
PREDICTION: The gradient regularized model is expected to achieve better performance than standard online learning methods, especially when faced with rapid changes in traffic patterns or noisy data. However, the optimal choice of regularization strength and sensitivity levels may depend on specific traffic characteristics, and improper tuning might lead to under-performance. To mitigate this, we will use techniques like cross-validation or active learning for tuning the hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE:  Online Multi-Step Traffic Flow Forecasting using Variational Autoencoders
PROPOSAL: We will explore the use of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) with online learning for multi-step traffic flow forecasting. The VAE will be trained to learn a compact and interpretable representation of the traffic flow patterns, allowing for more efficient online updates and better handling of delayed and noisy feedback.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will involve comparing the proposed VAE-based approach with existing online multi-step forecasting methods, such as online LSTM/NARX, and a single-step forecasting method with a highly complex architecture (e.g., a deep neural network with many layers).
COST: 50320
PREDICTION: The VAE-based approach is expected to achieve better multi-step forecasting performance than existing methods, particularly when faced with complex and changing traffic patterns. However, the VAE's ability to capture the underlying structure of the data may lead to over-smoothing or memorization of the data, and careful tuning of hyperparameters may be required to avoid these issues.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE:  Transfer Learning for Online Traffic Flow Forecasting with Domain Adversarial Training
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of domain adversarial training to adapt a pre-trained traffic flow forecasting model to new urban areas or changing traffic patterns. The model will be trained to predict both the traffic flow and the domain-specific features, and the domain adversarial loss will be used to align the predictions across different domains.
CONTROLS: Control experiments will be conducted using standard fine-tuning and transfer learning approaches, as well as domain adaptation methods without domain adversarial training.
COST: 32510
PREDICTION: The domain adversarial training approach is expected to improve the adaptation of the pre-trained model to new urban areas or changing traffic patterns, by learning a more general and domain-agnostic representation of the traffic flow patterns. However, the performance may degrade if the domain shift is too large or if the domain-specific features are not properly identified, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters and consideration of subspace alignment techniques.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE:  Transfer Learning for Online Traffic Flow Forecasting with Domain Adversarial Training and Ensemble Methods
PROPOSAL: We will revise the previous proposal by incorporating ensemble methods into the domain adversarial training framework. Specifically, we will use a combination of weighted average and bagging to combine the predictions from multiple models trained on different domains, with the goal of improving the overall adaptability and robustness of the model.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will include standard fine-tuning, transfer learning, and domain adaptation methods, as well as ensemble methods without domain adversarial training.
COST: 44830
PREDICTION: The revised approach is expected to improve the adaptability and robustness of the model to changing traffic patterns and new urban areas, by leveraging the strengths of both domain adversarial training and ensemble methods. However, the performance may degrade if the ensemble models are not properly combined or if the domain shift is too large, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters and consideration of methods for reducing overfitting and improving generalization.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE:  Multi-Agent Learning for Online Traffic Flow Forecasting with Communication between Agents
PROPOSAL: We will develop a multi-agent learning framework for online traffic flow forecasting, where multiple agents are placed at different locations along the road network and communicate with each other to share local traffic information. This will enable the agents to learn a more accurate and up-to-date representation of the traffic flow patterns, and make more informed predictions about future traffic conditions.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will involve comparing the proposed multi-agent learning approach with traditional single-agent methods, as well as methods that use communication but do not incorporate agent learning.
COST: 51650
PREDICTION: The multi-agent learning approach is expected to improve the accuracy and effectiveness of online traffic flow forecasting, by leveraging the strengths of both local and global traffic information. However, the performance may degrade if the communication between agents is not properly synchronized or if the agents have different levels of expertise, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters and consideration of methods for reducing information overload and improving agent cooperation.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE:  Uncertainty-Aware Online Time Series Forecasting using Bayesian Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: We will develop a Bayesian neural network framework for online time series forecasting, which can provide predictive uncertainty estimates about the future values of the time series. This will enable the model to better capture the uncertainty associated with the online learning process and make more informed decisions.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will involve comparing the proposed Bayesian neural network approach with traditional online time series forecasting methods, as well as methods that use uncertainty estimation but do not incorporate Bayesian neural networks.
COST: 63630
PREDICTION: The uncertainty-aware online time series forecasting approach is expected to improve the overall performance and reliability of the model, by providing more accurate uncertainty estimates and enabling more informed decision-making. However, the performance may degrade if the model is not properly configured to capture the underlying uncertainty structure of the data, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters and consideration of methods for reducing uncertainty overestimation.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE:  Robust Online Traffic Flow Forecasting against Concept Drift using Statistical Process Control
PROPOSAL: We will develop a statistical process control framework for robust online traffic flow forecasting against concept drift. The framework will monitor the performance of the model and detect changes in the underlying data distribution, triggering a shift in the model's parameters to adapt to the new concept.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will involve comparing the proposed statistical process control approach with traditional online traffic flow forecasting methods, as well as methods that use concept drift detection but do not incorporate statistical process control.
COST: 67290
PREDICTION: The robust online traffic flow forecasting approach is expected to improve the model's ability to adapt to changing traffic patterns and concept drift, by providing a more accurate and timely detection of shifts in the underlying data distribution. However, the performance may degrade if the model is not properly configured to detect changes in the data distribution or if the concept drift is too rapid, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters and consideration of methods for reducing false positives and false negatives.

TITLE:  Evaluating the Transferability of Online Traffic Flow Forecasting Models across Different Cities and Routes
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an in-depth evaluation of the transferability of online traffic flow forecasting models across different cities and routes. We will train and test models on various datasets from different locations and assess their performance in terms of accuracy, robustness, and adaptability.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will involve comparing the transferability of the proposed models with traditional models that are not specifically designed for transfer learning.
COST: 76540
PREDICTION: The evaluation of transferability is expected to provide insights into the portability and adaptability of online traffic flow forecasting models across different cities and routes, highlighting limitations and areas for improvement. However, the performance may degrade if the models are not properly configured to capture local and regional patterns, or if the datasets are not adequately representative of the target locations.

PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive comparison of the proposed online traffic flow forecasting methods in a real-world urban environment, using a large and diverse dataset from multiple cities. We will evaluate the performance of each method in terms of accuracy, robustness, and adaptability, and identify the strengths and limitations of each approach.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Hybrid Retrieval with Multimodal Late Interaction
PROPOSAL: This experiment compares the performance of the baseline ColPali-based encoder with a hybrid retriever approach that aggregates the output of the ColPali-based encoder with a lightweight dense text retriever. We will use a combination of logistic regression and element-wise multiplication as the aggregation method. We will evaluate the hybrid approach on the visdorm benchmark, a public visual document retrieval benchmark, using Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) and Recall at 10 (R@10) as the metrics.
CONTROLS: 1) Baseline: ColPali-based encoder alone, 2) Ablation: lightweight dense text retriever alone, 3) Baseline for text retriever: BM25, 4) Extrapolation: applying late interaction to text representations instead of aggregating text and image retrievers
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The hybrid approach should improve MRR and R@10 over the baseline, with a margin of 1-2% relatively, and may fail if the aggregation method is too simple to capture complex interactions between the multimodal representations.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Designing Multimodal Representation Fusion Schemes
PROPOSAL: This work investigates various methods for fusing the representations of the text retriever and the ColPali-based encoder. Specifically, we will experiment with MODE ( Multiplicative Operation based Deep fusion Ecology), late interaction fusion, and an attention-based fusion scheme, comparing their performance on the visdorm benchmark. We will also examine the impact of different dimensionalities for the representations of the two models before fusion.
CONTROLS: 1) Baseline: direct concatenation of representations, 2) Comparison: Modality-Specific Relevance-Free Representations, 3) Extrapolation: applying multimodal representation fusion schemes to other paired multimodal retrieval tasks
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The attention-based fusion scheme will outperform MODE and late interaction fusion by 1-2% relatively on MRR and R@10, and might fail if it is overly sensitive to hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Query Representation in Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with learning query-specific transformations to make the text retriever's query representation more compatible with the ColPali-based encoder's multimodal representations. This will involve using a multi-task learning objective, where the primary task is document ranking and the auxiliary task is query representation alignment.
CONTROLS: 1) Baseline: fixed query representation, 2) Ablation: no query representation alignment, 3) Comparison: query-specific transformations learned through self-supervised learning, and 4) Extrapolation: applying query-specific transformations to other multimodal retrieval tasks
COST: 540
PREDICTION: The multi-task learning objective will lead to improved performance on MRR and R@10, especially when combined with effective representation fusion schemes, but might fail if the auxiliary task becomes too dominant.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Query Representation in Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: This experiment extends the query representation transformation design by introducing a progressive ranking module to selectively emphasize query-related information in the transformation process. We will also compare the effectiveness of different distance metrics (e.g., cosine similarity, L2 distance) in measuring the alignment between query representations of the text retriever and the ColPali-based encoder.
CONTROLS: 1) Baseline: fixed query representation, 2) Ablation: no query representation alignment, 3) Comparison: query-specific transformations with global average pooling, 4) Comparison: query-specific transformations with progressive ranking module, and 5) Extrapolation: applying query-specific transformations to other multimodal retrieval tasks
COST: 720
PREDICTION: The progressive ranking module will lead to further improvements in MRR and R@10, and the best distance metric will be identified, but might fail if the progressive ranking module introduces additional noise into the system.
